newsitem.title: USA: Veteran detective added to JonBenet case.
newsitem.headline: Veteran detective added to JonBenet case.

text.p: A veteran detective who has investigated more than 150 homicide cases has been added to the team trying to find out who murdered 6-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey, officials said Thursday.

Retired detective Andrew Louis "Lou" Smit, 61, will join a task force assembled to investigate the killing and help prepare a prosecution case, Boulder spokesman Kelvin McNeill announced at a weekly briefing.
No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the 12-week-old probe.
Smit, from Colorado Springs, has investigated several high-profile Colorado cases, including the 1975 murder of five people, one of whom was Karen Grammer, sister of television star Kelsey Grammer.
The body of JonBenet Ramsey was found Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's home in Boulder about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
McNeill said a Boulder detective recently travelled to Charlevoix, Michigan, where the Ramsey family has a summer home. He declined to disclose what was obtained under a search warrant.
